newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ CHEs' revenue from government up in Dec qtr.
newsitem.headline: NZ CHEs' revenue from government up in Dec qtr.

text.p: Crown Health Enterprises received NZ$17.6 million more revenue from the government in the December 1996 quarter than in the December 1995 quarter, Statistics New Zealand said on Tuesday.

"Government revenue has increased from $636.6 million in the December 1995 quarter to $654.2 million in the latest quarter. This was the main reason for the 2.5 percent, or $17.3 million rise in total CHE income," SNZ said.
Total revenue for the CHEs was $716.9 million in the December 1996 quarter.

Despite the increased revenue, the CHEs recorded a combined deficit of $50.5 million in the December 1996 quarter, $22.1 million higher than the deficit of $28.4 million recorded in the December 1995 quarter.

SNZ said this worsening deficit could be attributed to a smaller increase in income when compared to the increase in expenditure: the total cost of providing services rose by $39.4 million, or 5.4 percent, between the December 1995 and December 1996 quarters.
